summary.headline: KP Green Engineering FY26 revenue rose 78% to INR1,250 crore and EBITDA 117% to INR249 crore, with INR1,831 crore order book slated for FY27 execution.
summary.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue of INR1,250 crore (up 78%), EBITDA of INR249 crore (up 117%, margin ~20% vs 16%) and PAT of INR136 crore (up 85%). H2 FY26 consolidated total income was INR714 crore (up 64% YoY) with PAT of INR77 crore (up 68%). Capacity utilisation remained low at about 30-34% on 4,00,500 MTPA capacity, with management guiding to 40-60% in FY27. Working capital rose sharply on inventory build-up tied to geopolitical fuel and raw material risk, and short-term borrowings increased. Management reiterated 40-50% annual growth and a 16-20% EBITDA margin range for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY vs INR115 crore; margin from 16%

segments.name: Transmission line towers
segments.commentary: Approved and active across 16+ states; power and transmission is the largest current sector focus per management.

segments.name: Telecom (BSNL)
segments.commentary: Single largest order: INR819+ crore BSNL telecom tower order with O&M annuity potential; management says it is the majority of the order book being executed.

segments.name: Solar structures and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Approved by Nextracker and GameChange Solar; RDSO approval achieved for railways. Solar was cited by an analyst as a historically heavy share but no split was given.

segments.name: Galvanizing (Matar)
segments.commentary: Asia's largest hot-dip galvanizing plant, 90,000 MTPA with 15 MT single-dip capacity, now operational.

guidance_outlook: Entire INR1,800+ crore order book expected to be executed in FY27 (confirmed by management).
Growth guidance of minimum 40-50% YoY, with no upper limit if capacity allows; management declined to commit to 100% growth.
EBITDA margin to be maintained in 16-20% range in FY27, subject to fuel, raw material and geopolitical pressures.
Capacity utilisation expected at 40%-60% in FY27 versus 30-34% at present.
Next phase capex to be mainly backward integration (rolling mill) with operations in FY27; described as nascent and at discussion stage.
Bidding pipeline above INR3,000 crore with 60-70% stated success ratio in tenders.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 4,00,500 MTPA; FY26 production was about 1,24,500 MT.
Capacity utilisation 30-34% at present; management expects 40%-60% in FY27.
Asia's largest hot-dip galvanizing plant commissioned at Matar: 90,000 MTPA, 15 MT single dip.

Next capex phase mainly backward integration, e.g. rolling mill, with operations expected in FY27; cable and conductor, aluminium extrusion, fasteners, containers, onshore and offshore tubular towers also in pipeline.
Earlier capex funded by IPO proceeds (management cited INR190 crore as the IPO size).
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,831 crore as on 31 March 2026, including an INR500 crore order received around 1 May 2026; management said the INR1,800 crore figure already includes it.
Management said the order book is stated in the PPT on a won basis, but BSE disclosure is made only after LOA is received.
Internal group company share of order book is 22-25%; rest is external.
Galvanizing plant energy: green hydrogen blended up to 20-25% into LPG, reducing cost only marginally; management cites ESG and speed benefits.
Raw material escalation above 5% is passed through in large contracts; smaller contracts rely on inventory and hedging.
Management said H1 revenue exceeded H2 partly due to fuel constraints and customer billing timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book INR1,800 crore plus INR500 crore, and when will it execute?
qa_highlights.answer: Total order book including the INR500 crore is about INR1,800 crore as on date, and the entire book is to be executed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY26 capacity utilisation and FY27 outlook? What is the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 utilisation was 1,24,500 MT of 4,00,500 MTPA. FY27 growth minimum 40-50%; EBITDA margin to be kept in 16-20% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from about 96 to 195 days and what happened to cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up as a hedge against geopolitical price and availability risk, using working capital limits. Cash fell because FDs over one year were reclassified to other financial assets (around INR59 crore FY26 vs INR52 crore FY25); operating cash flow was INR155 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt rising and is the company planning to become debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is mainly short-term working capital; long-term debt has not risen. Average cost 8.5-9%, rated A. No plan to become debt-free currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why are related-party royalties charged at 2% and what is the cricket sponsorship?
qa_highlights.answer: Royalty at 2% of top line is paid for group brand building that is done by the promoter; cricket sponsorship is brand-level and is expensed by the promoter, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cable and conductor plan, and will revenue come from outside the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable and conductor is aimed primarily at external power and transmission customers, with group supply as a secondary use.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to quarterly reporting, and when is Main Board migration?
qa_highlights.answer: Half-yearly reporting is mandatory; management will review quarterly reporting with the board. Main Board listing to follow once SEBI criteria are met.

risks_watch: Working capital and inventory: inventory days rose sharply to about 195 days; utilisation of working capital limits is fully drawn.
Fuel and gas supply for galvanizing and machinery under geopolitical stress; management says it is the main execution concern.
Margin dependence on raw material pass-through; only contracts above 5% escalation are passed on and other contracts rely on inventory hedging.
Related-party royalty at 2% of revenue paid to promoter-linked entity; group orders 20-25% of order book.
Revenue visibility depends on conversion of pipeline (INR2,000-3,000 crore) and on LOA timing versus win disclosure.
Reporting: only half-yearly results; cash and other financial asset reclassification may confuse comparability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, but evasive on specifics such as FY27 margin, capex size and quantification of the inventory build-up. Management repeatedly hedged with phrases like the margin range "we cannot assure" and the defence and quarterly reporting items being at discussion stage.
